inline_comments.comment:
The `Number.isInteger` guard is overly strict: any positive non-integer float (e.g., `maxPresetColors: 3.5`) fails the check and silently falls back to 27, which is surprising and undocumented. Since `color` quantities are always whole numbers in practice, prefer truncating the value and validating the result:

```ts
const limit = Number.isFinite(maxPresetColors) && maxPresetColors > 0
  ? Math.trunc(maxPresetColors)
  : 27;
```
This also makes `Infinity` correctly fall through to the guard on line 335 instead of needing a separate special-case check there.

The JSDoc documents `0` and `Infinity` as escape hatches but is silent about what happens with other invalid inputs (negative numbers, non-integer floats). Both silently fall back to 27. Adding a sentence — e.g., "Any other non-positive or non-integer value is treated as invalid and falls back to `27`" — would make the contract explicit and prevent confusion for callers who accidentally pass a float or negative value.

The `WithInvalidMaxPresetColors` story claims to demonstrate "falls back to 27" but only supplies 5 preset colors. Because 5 < 27, the rendered output is identical to any normal 5-color story regardless of what `maxPresetColors` is set to — the fallback is invisible. To actually exercise and visually verify the fallback, supply more than 27 preset colors; then the story would show 27 while a story without the invalid value shows all of them.

The three new stories rely on `startOpen: true` to show the open state for visual regression testing, but none include a `play` function. Per project guidelines, interactive component stories (pickers, popovers, expandable sections) should drive interaction programmatically via a `play` function so the open/expanded state is reliably captured in visual tests. `startOpen` is a convenience prop, not a substitute — it bypasses the real open/close code path. A `play` function that clicks the color swatch to open the picker would also verify the toggle interaction itself.

general_comments.comment: There are no unit tests for the new `maxPresetColors` logic in `usePresets`. The stories provide visual coverage, but they do not programmatically assert edge cases like `0` (no limit), `Infinity` (no limit), a negative value (fallback to 27), `NaN`, or a non-integer float. A unit test file (or additions to an existing one) that directly tests the slicing/fallback behavior would make future regressions immediately obvious and document the intended semantics more precisely than stories alone.
